correctness.rationale: For every fixed finite reflexive rooted star, structural induction reduces truth to root color and leaf-color support. Explicit depth-two formulas recover each admissible nonuniform root support and identify uniform roots with leaf colors; distinct types have characteristic formulas. Boolean closure gives exactly 2 to the pointed-type count, while depth one sees only root color plus accessible palette. Concrete two-support witnesses prove sharpness and absence-profile witnesses prove exact branching cutoffs. All boundaries s=0 and k=0 are handled. Exhaustive pointed-model refinement (24686 cases) and independent direct term closure (4,16,64,64) passed from packaged verify.py; finite checks corroborate but are not infinite proof.

claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: A generic Hennessy–Milner theorem identifies types after a bisimulation partition is already determined; it does not itself enumerate possible profiles over all valuations. The topological theorem counts strictly more profiles using a different primitive and hence provides no equality in this reduct. The intuitionistic theorem excludes arbitrary Boolean valuations. The chain theorem has different accessibility and no branching. The candidate combines a complete explicit observation basis, all-variable algebra cardinalities, and distinct sharp saturation steps not deducible as a stated corollary from those inspected claims.

value.rationale: This solves a natural complete classification problem for fixed finite S4 modal Boolean formula algebras for every variable and branching parameter. It identifies a sharp structural source of depth-two expressivity and a last-leaf distinction invisible to depth one; this is an exact invariant and boundary, not a routine renaming, isolated tiny numerical gain, or generic local-finiteness fact.
